analysis.title: UBS TECH DAILY CURT COMMENT: Interesting Monday comment, CAP, AMZN, Intel
key_insights: Intel fell 23% on a weaker PC segment and AMZN fell 7% on a revenue miss. ServiceNow (NOW) fell 27% the prior day. The author says the bounce is hard earned but gravity is gravity.

Monday.com (MNDY) credit-based AI pricing is creating friction. Several customers are limiting usage because consumption is unpredictable. One customer used 200K credits in two days against a 100K allotment, and another used its monthly allocation halfway through the month.

Customers for whom AI is more needle-moving expect spend increases of 10-15%. SMBs are less willing to pay for AI. There was little evidence of customers swapping seats for credits, so credit spend is largely incremental today.

Capgemini (Neutral, PT EUR 107) Q3 sales were EUR 6,073m, up 11.7% in constant currency, about 5.5% organic, against Street EUR 5,999m, 3.9% organic and 10.5% constant currency. This is a roughly 1% revenue beat. The stock is expected flattish to down small. UBS calls it more a call on market and semi-versus-software factors.

Capgemini Q3 bookings rose 3.4% in constant currency. FY organic growth guide is 4-4.5% and constant-currency growth 9-9.5% (was 8.5-9%), against Street 4.1% organic and 9.1% constant currency. Margin guide of 13.6-13.8% and organic FCF guide of EUR 1.8-1.9bn were reiterated.

Intel guided well below even the most bearish investor expectations because of a much worse PC segment. PC revenue was $8.1B (-9% Q/Q, -5% Y/Y). Higher memory prices, limited availability and constrained IT budgets weakened PC sell-through and caused a sharper late-quarter OEM inventory correction.
UBS sees no relief in sight for memory pricing and supply, especially as server demand for agentic applications grows. The path to PC recovery looks challenging.

UBS expects Intel capex to rise at least 50% in C2027, and Intel is adding substrate capacity for servers. UBS does not think this should dampen enthusiasm for foundry (Apple CPU as the first big engagement, in UBS's view), advanced packaging, server and ASIC.

UBS cuts Intel C2027 estimates but still sees about $3 EPS as doable for C2028 and over $4 for C2029. Terafab process technology sharing could add longer-term optionality, and UBS thinks Intel ultimately has to get a license. At a mid-to-high 20x P/E there is little room for multiple expansion, so the market needs to roll its basis forward to C2029. PT is cut to $80 and the rating stays Neutral.

Read-across to AMD is negative but tempered. If notebook and desktop units fall about 25% Q/Q in the December quarter, UBS estimates about $700MM of revenue is removed from each of FQ4 (Dec) and FQ1 (Mar), which would bring UBS numbers just in line with the Street, since UBS thinks the Street was too low. Read-across to semicaps is neutral because Intel's capex message was unchanged.

AMZN fell 7% after hours on an AWS revenue miss. AWS grew 39% Y/Y against investor expectations of 42-43% (bogey 44-45%). AWS margin was 38.7% against a bogey in the low 40s. Informal guidance calls for AWS growth over 40% in both FY27 and FY28.
AMZN Q3 NA retail growth was 6%, in line with the bogey. Q3 EBIT was $28.1B (13.9% margin) against a bogey of $27-28B, in line. Q3 total sales were $202B against a bogey of $204-205B, a miss.
AMZN Q4 EBIT guide is $28.5-33.5B against a bogey of $31-35B, and the Q4 sales guide is $240-247B against a bogey of $241-248B. Both are misses. FY26 capex guidance of $220B was reiterated.

AMZN management cited good AWS visibility into 2027 and 2028 and some into 2029. It called AI a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity and said it will keep investing to lead. It said it can fund the plan and that FCF will change in the future.

STMicro Q4 gross-margin guidance surprised positively at 39%, despite 40bps of unused-capacity charges and 30bps of manufacturing-efficiency headwinds. Management expects Q1 margin at least in line with 38% consensus (UBSe 38.6%). The manufacturing programme should add about 400bps by end-2027 or early 2028. UBS expects gross margin above 45% by 2028E against 43% consensus.

UBS stress-tests STM with AI revenue halving by 2028E on hyperscaler cuts or share loss, which cuts AI EPS to about $0.5 from $1.0 in UBS estimates. STM would still earn about $3.5 EPS, including $3.0 from non-AI, about 30% below the 2023 peak. Applying 10x to ex-AI earnings, against 14.9x historical 2Y forward, implies about $30-35 per share, or 15-20% downside.

UBS Evidence Lab data on iPhone availability across 30+ geographies shows wait times for the iPhone Duo down 7 days WoW but still elevated at about 89 days on average. Display issue reports are a concern but UBS does not think they are the main driver of the declining wait times. Pro wait times fell 3 days WoW and Pro Max was unchanged, similar to last year's models, and UBS expects Pro and Pro Max wait times to fall next week.

market_movers.rationale: Q3 revenue beat the Street by about 1% and FY constant-currency growth guidance was raised to 9-9.5%. UBS says there is nothing much to see and expects the stock flattish to down small.

PT is cut to $80 after a weak PC segment and guidance below even the most bearish expectations. UBS still sees about $3 EPS in C2028 and over $4 in C2029, but the mid-to-high 20x P/E leaves little room for multiple expansion.
Shares fell 7% after hours. AWS growth of 39% missed expectations of 42-43%, AWS margin missed, and the Q4 EBIT and sales guides came in below the bogey.
Weaker PC units read negatively for FQ4 and FQ1 revenue. A roughly 25% Q/Q unit drop would remove about $700MM per quarter, though that would only bring UBS numbers in line with the Street.

sector_views.rationale: Intel's capex message was unchanged, so the read-across to semicaps is neutral. PC weakness is negative for AMD, and memory pricing and supply are not expected to ease.

earnings_insights: Intel reported PC segment revenue of $8.1B (-9% Q/Q, -5% Y/Y), below expectations. Guidance was well below even the most bearish investor expectations. The stock fell 23%.

AMZN reported (Q3, printed) AWS growth of 39% Y/Y against a bogey of 44-45%. AWS margin was 38.7% against a bogey in the low 40s. Total sales were $202B against a bogey of $204-205B and guidance of $197-202B. EBIT was $28.1B against a bogey of $27-28B and guidance of $22.5-26.5B.
AMZN Q4 guidance: EBIT $28.5-33.5B against a bogey of $31-35B, and total sales $240-247B against a bogey of $241-248B. FY26 capex guide of $220B was reiterated.

Capgemini reported (Q3, printed 10/30) sales of EUR 6,073m against Street EUR 5,999m, with organic growth of about 5.5% against Street 3.9%. Bookings rose 3.4% in constant currency. FY guide: organic 4-4.5% against Street 4.1%, constant currency 9-9.5% (was 8.5-9%) against Street 9.1%. Margin of 13.6-13.8% and organic FCF of EUR 1.8-1.9bn were reiterated, against Street margin 13.6% and FCF EUR 1,863m.
STMicro guided Q4 gross margin to 39% and Q1 margin at least in line with the 38% consensus (UBSe 38.6%). UBS expects gross margin above 45% by 2028E against 43% consensus.
Monday.com (MNDY) customer checks show AI credit-based pricing friction and SMB reluctance to pay for AI. These come from UBS channel checks, not reported results.
risk_factors: Memory pricing and supply constraints, with no relief seen, are hurting PC sell-through and OEM inventories.
AI monetization in software is held back by unpredictable credit-based pricing, limited cost visibility and SMB reluctance to pay.
Hyperscaler capex cuts or share loss could halve STM's AI revenue by 2028E.
Display issue reports on the iPhone Duo are a concern, though UBS does not see them as the main driver of the wait-time decline.
Intel's higher capex (up at least 50% in C2027, in UBS's view) and its mid-to-high 20x P/E limit upside.
vol_and_positioning: The author notes ServiceNow fell 27% the prior day, Intel fell 23% and AMZN fell 7% after hours, and says the bounce is hard earned but gravity is gravity.

tension_points.bull_case: Capex and substrate additions support foundry (Apple CPU as first big engagement in UBS's view), advanced packaging, server and ASIC. UBS sees about $3 EPS in C2028 and over $4 in C2029, and sustained PC weakness may let Intel push its server roadmap faster.
tension_points.bear_case: PC revenue was $8.1B (-9% Q/Q, -5% Y/Y) with no relief seen in memory pricing and supply. At a mid-to-high 20x P/E there is little room for multiple expansion.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The market needs to roll its basis forward to C2029 for the stock to start working again.

tension_points.bull_case: Gross margin is expected above 45% by 2028E and the manufacturing programme adds about 400bps by end-2027 or early 2028.
tension_points.bear_case: AI revenue could halve by 2028E on hyperscaler cuts or share loss, cutting AI EPS to about $0.5 from $1.0.
